'''Austin Gerard Smith''' (born 1960) is a professor at the [[University of Exeter]] and director of its Living Systems Institute.<ref name="LSI">{{cite web|title=Professor Austin Smith FRS, Exeter|url=https://www.exeter.ac.uk/livingsystems/team/profile/index.php?web_id=Austin_Smith}}</ref> He is notable for his pioneering work on the biology of [[embryonic stem cells]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.businessweek.com/magazine/content/02_24/b3787622.htm |work=Businessweek |title=The Stars of Europe – Innovators: Austin Smith, Director, Centre for Genome Research |date=17 June 2002 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080531001902/http://www.businessweek.com/magazine/content/02_24/b3787622.htm |archive-date=31 May 2008 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url =https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2009/02/090227112303.htm | work = Science Daily | title= New Safer Way Developed To Reprogram Stem Cells | date = 3 March 2009}}</ref>

==Education==
Austin Smith obtained his doctoral degree from the [[University of Edinburgh]] in 1986.<ref name="SCI">{{cite journal | last1=Kalkan | first1=Tüzer | last2=Olova | first2=Nelly | last3=Roode | first3=Mila | last4=Mulas | first4=Carla | last5=Lee | first5=Heather J. | last6=Nett | first6=Isabelle | last7=Marks | first7=Hendrik | last8=Walker | first8=Rachael | last9=Stunnenberg | first9=Hendrik G. | last10=Lilley | first10=Kathryn S. | last11=Nichols | first11=Jennifer | last12=Reik | first12=Wolf | last13=Bertone | first13=Paul | last14=Smith | first14=Austin | title=Tracking the embryonic stem cell transition from ground state pluripotency | journal=Development | publisher=The Company of Biologists | volume=144 | issue=7 | date=1 April 2017 | issn=1477-9129 | doi=10.1242/dev.142711 | pages=1221–1234| pmid=28174249 | pmc=5399622 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Austin Gerard|first=Smith|date=1986|title=Genetic analysis of embryonal carcinoma cells|hdl=1842/20194|publisher=[[University of Edinburgh]]|url=https://www.era.lib.ed.ac.uk/handle/1842/20194|language=en}}</ref>

==Career and research==
He then carried out [[postdoctoral research]] at the [[University of Oxford]], before joining the Centre for Genome Research at the [[University of Edinburgh]] as a group leader.<ref name="SCI" /> In 1996, he was appointed director of the centre, which became the Institute for Stem Cell Research under his leadership.<ref name="SCI" /> He remained as director of the Institute until his move to Cambridge in 2006.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.wellcome.ac.uk/News/Media-office/Press-releases/2006/WTX032909.htm |title=Stage set for world-leading stem cell research centre |publisher=Wellcome Trust |access-date=5 September 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120320023500/http://www.wellcome.ac.uk/News/Media-office/Press-releases/2006/WTX032909.htm |archive-date=20 March 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Here, he became a director of the Welcome Trust Centre for Stem Cell Research <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cam.ac.uk/news/stage-set-for-world-leading-stem-cell-research-centre |title=Stage set for world-leading stem cell research centre &#124; University of Cambridge |website=Cam.ac.uk |date=2006-07-25 |access-date=2017-06-25}}</ref> and later was the director of the new Wellcome Trust-MRC [[Cambridge Stem Cell Institute]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], which was established with 8 million pounds ($12.5 million) awarded by the [[Wellcome Trust]] and [[Medical Research Council (UK)]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite news| url= https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2012-08-08/cambridge-joins-harvard-in-opening-stem-cell-institute.html | work= Bloomberg News | title= Cambridge Joins Harvard In Opening Stem-Cell Institute | date=8 August 2012}}</ref>

In 2019, he was appointed as the new Director of the University of Exeter's Living Systems Institute.<ref name="LSI"/>

In 2003, Smith was awarded an MRC Research Professorship<ref name="SCI" /> and elected to the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]].<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/fellowship/fellows.pdf|title= RSE Fellows as at 12/04/2011|publisher= Royal Society of Edinburgh|access-date= 26 April 2011|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110517011845/http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/fellowship/fellows.pdf|archive-date= 17 May 2011|url-status= dead}}</ref> And in 2006, was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]].<ref>{{cite web| url = http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/fellows/|title= Fellows|publisher= Royal Society|access-date= 4 December 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101130205758/http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/fellows/| archive-date= 30 November 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> In 2010, he was co-recipient of the [[Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine]] along with French cardiologist [[Michel Haissaguerre]].<ref name="Louis-Jeantet">{{cite web|url=http://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2010-01/embo-2lp012510.php |title=2010 Louis-Jeantet prize for medicine &#124; EurekAlert! Science News |website=Eurekalert.org |date= |access-date=2017-06-25}}</ref>

In February 2010, together with 13 other leading stem cell researchers, he wrote an open letter to journal editors to voice the opinion that obstructive reviews by a small number of researchers in the field were hindering publication of novel stem cell research.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.eurostemcell.org/commentanalysis/peer-review |title= Open letter to Senior Editors of peer-review journals publishing in the field of stem cell biology
|access-date= 5 September 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/8490291.stm | work=BBC News | first=Pallab | last=Ghosh | title=Journal stem cell work 'blocked' | date=2 February 2010}}</ref>
